title: Logger cannot be initialized
summary: The recurring logger initialization popup is a valid symptom, but the trigger is intermittent and the diagnostic archive was rejected. The author reports that it may occur while opening a file and disappears when PowerToys is not running, which is not enough to identify affected components or a reproducible path.

status.label: needs information
status.detail: Request a valid diagnostic archive and a controlled reproduction identifying the triggering PowerToys component or file operation.

judgment.rationale: The recurring logger initialization popup is a valid symptom, but the trigger is intermittent and the diagnostic archive was rejected. The author reports that it may occur while opening a file and disappears when PowerToys is not running, which is not enough to identify affected components or a reproducible path.
evidence: The body reports recurring "Logger cannot be initialized" popups on PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store.
The issue includes a screenshot and a diagnostic ZIP, but automated triage reports the archive was rejected because of an oversized entry.
The author says the issue can be absent for hours, then recur, and possibly occurs when opening a file.
The author says the problem stops when PowerToys is not running.
Related issue #27104 is closed with Resolution-Can't Repro, but no public evidence establishes that it is the same current failure.
judgment.recommended_action: Request a valid diagnostic archive and a controlled reproduction identifying the triggering PowerToys component or file operation.

comment.body:
Please provide a newly generated, valid PowerToys bug report ZIP captured immediately after the popup appears. Also record:

- The exact local date and time of one or more occurrences.
- Which PowerToys utilities are enabled and whether the popup appears while opening a file, browsing folders, or using a specific utility.
- The file type, application, and action being performed when the popup appears, if applicable.
- Whether the popup occurs in a clean session after disabling individual PowerToys utilities, and which utility was last disabled before the behavior stopped.
- Whether the issue reproduces with PowerToys started normally versus as administrator.
- The complete error text from the popup and any Windows Event Viewer or PowerToys log entries from the same timestamp.

Please confirm whether the issue still reproduces on the latest stable PowerToys release.
